text:
The season in Chicago keeps circling back to Connor Bedard's right shoulder. He was hurt again in the Nov. 17 win over Toronto, his third shoulder injury in less than a year, and the Blackhawks have been weighing surgery against rehab with no timeline set, according to TSN. That is the story, and it hangs over everything else.

What's happened without him has been oddly lively. Sunday's 6-3 win in Vancouver was 4-0 before the Canucks had a shot, as Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis noted, with a Roman Kantserov hat trick and three power-play goals. Sam Rinzel has 14 points in his last 10 games against 5.8 expected, a run that put him alongside Orr, Salming and Howe for straight multi-assist games. Frank Nazar (11 points in 10) and Kantserov are running hot too, and Patrick Kane, back in Chicago on a two-year deal, has six points in a four-game streak.

The team underneath is still thin. Chicago is 8-14-2 with 43% of the expected goals, and the Wyatt Kaiser and Artyom Levshunov pair has been outscored 15-4. Arvid Soderblom has stopped .846 over his last four starts. Our race model gives Jeff Blashill's team essentially no playoff chance, projecting about 69 points.

What to watch: whether the young scorers keep producing once the hot finishing cools, and what the club decides about Bedard's shoulder.
headline: Bedard hurt again, and the kids keep scoring
